subject: SIG: Deprovisioning provenance and SCIM playbook for MedBridge intake
messages:
From: Alice Nguyen <alice.nguyen@medbridge.com>
To: Alex Martinez <alex@redwood.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 18 Jul 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: SIG intake — need deprovisioning provenance and SCIM deltas

Alex —

We are doing the security intake for our upcoming SIG questionnaire and need a tight package showing how Redwood handles deprovisioning for SSO/SAML accounts. Specifically MedBridge needs the following artifacts for the last 90 days:

- SCIM delta export (format: CSV preferred) showing remove/disable events with timestamps and user IDs
- Representative SAML assertion(s) that show how user status is reflected on logout/deprovision (redact PII as needed)
- A short playbook (step-by-step) describing the deprovisioning flow from IdP change -> SCIM event -> RBAC enforcement -> access removal in runtime
- Evidence that roles are pruned (RBAC role map snapshot) for accounts that were removed

Can you deliver a bundle we can attach to the SIG / CAIQ response? If possible, include a small timeline for one deprovisioning example (timestamped events) and call out any automated rollback/fallback behaviors.

We will need any user-level identifiers redacted for public share; please advise your redaction approach. Also include any retention policies that would affect log availability.

Thanks — happy to jump on a 20-min call if helpful.

Alice Nguyen
Security Programs Manager
MedBridge Health
security@medbridge.com
From: Alex Martinez <alex@redwood.com>
To: Alice Nguyen <alice.nguyen@medbridge.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 19 Jul 2027 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: SIG intake — need deprovisioning provenance and SCIM deltas

Hi Alice —

Thanks for the clear list. We can produce the bundle you outlined. High-level plan:

1) Export SCIM delta CSV for the requested window (we'll include change-type, timestamp (UTC), scimId, externalId, `action` field where action\u003dremove/replace/disable).
2) Package SAML assertion samples (we will include the assertion headers and the NameID/attributes mapping that indicate account status) — PII will be redacted per your guidance.
3) Generate a short deprovisioning playbook (PDF) that maps the IdP event to our internal job IDs and the resulting role removals.
4) RBAC role map snapshot (JSON) plus a human-readable summar y of role owners and least-privilege checks.

Deliverables will be placed on a shared Drive folder and we'll attach copies in email. A couple of quick clarifying questions before we run the export:

- For redaction: do you want full email addresses removed or pseudonymized (e.g., user-12345)?
- Are you okay with a 90-day window ending 2027-07-18? If you need a different window please let us know.

I will coordinate with Karthik and Priyom on the SCIM and RBAC pieces; target delivery is EOD Wed (2027-07-21). If we need to accelerate we'll set a short meeting.

Regards,

Alex Martinez
Sr. Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
attachments: scim-delta-request-template.txt
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
To: Alex Martinez <alex@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.com>
Cc: Alice Nguyen <alice.nguyen@medbridge.com>
Date: Tue, 20 Jul 2027 08:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: SIG intake — need deprovisioning provenance and SCIM deltas

Folks —

Technical note and contents I'm preparing for the bundle (we will drop these into the Drive link Alex created):

- scim-delta-20270701-20270718.csv (columns: event_id, scimId, externalId, username, action, timestamp_utc, initiated_by, source_system) — we will pseudonymize username -> user-<sha256 prefix> unless MedBridge requests full redaction.
- saml-assertions-deprovisioning.zip (contains 3 assertion text files: assertion-20270602.txt, assertion-20270623.txt, assertion-20270710.txt). Each contains the raw <Assertion> header and a redaction log showing which attributes were scrubbed.
- rbac-role-map-202707.json (role -> permission list; owners; last_modified). We'll also include a 1-page role-pruning summary noting any roles removed during the 90-day window.
- deprov-playbook-medbridge.pdf (short playbook: IdP change -> SCIM event -> worker job ID -> runtime revocation -> cache invalidation -> post-check within 5 minutes; includes rollback if SCIM delta fails)
- retention-policy.txt (pointer to our logs retention policy and where audit exports are stored)

A few implementation details to call out in the playbook: our SCIM worker writes events to an append-only events table; deprovisioning events trigger a job that updates role assignments in the authz service and asynchronously invalidates user sessions in the runtime by publishing a token-revocation event. Typical end-to-end completion for a remove event is under 5 minutes in normal conditions; we'll include a sampled timeline with timestamps from a real deprovisioning case.

I'll attach the artifacts to email for the SIG bundle and add the Drive links. Alex — will you handle the final zip and redaction?

- Karthik

---
Karthik Iyer
Principal Engineer, Platform Security
Redwood Inference
From: Alice Nguyen <alice.nguyen@medbridge.com>
To: Alex Martinez <alex@redwood.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 21 Jul 2027 15:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: SIG intake — need deprovisioning provenance and SCIM deltas

Alex / Karthik —

Perfect, thanks for the quick turnaround and the clear artifact list. Pseudonymized identifiers (user-12345) are fine for our public SIG package; for the auditors we may request a sealed copy with real identifiers under an NDA — we'll flag that later if needed.

Please include the sampled timeline (timestamps) and the retention-policy.txt in the shared folder. Also include a short note on who to contact if we spot a deprovisioning discrepancy (name + email).

Can we do a 20-minute sync tomorrow (Thu 2027-07-22) at 10:00 AM PT to walk through the folder and confirm redaction? If that works, I'll send a calendar invite.

Thanks —
Alice
